0:00–0:50
We built chRNA evidence review for scientists deciding which chimeric-RNA junction to test next. A chimeric RNA joins parts of two genes. A ranked gene pair is useful, but an experiment needs an exact junction and a reason to trust that junction.
Our starting point is a published mouse-macrophage dataset, not a claim that we discovered new functional proteins. We reconstructed 479 eligible probe-panel pairs and preserved the distinction between reported support and unknown biological truth.
The problem we focus on is the review decision: when a score, a probe and the evidence disagree, what should the scientist do next?

Sources: repository results/dataset_reconstruction/audit.md and manifest.json; Venezia et al. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10982-x

0:50–2:00
Codex reviewed three selected cases. It chose bounded tools, inspected returned results, and wrote a source-linked next-step proposal. We retained the actual calls, outputs and source hashes. The page replays those recorded runs; it is not a live model call.
The tools compare published read and probe endpoints, re-match genuine NVIDIA Parabricks output, inspect available structure evidence, and retrieve fixed primary-paper passages. The Parabricks run aligned two million paired reads on an A100. Our review reuses that real output; we did not run new GPUs to decorate the demo.
All twelve recorded outputs recompute exactly. The scientist can inspect the evidence and endorse, revise or defer the next step. A local review receipt is bound to the specific decision. It is self-reported and is not proof of biological validation.

Source: scripts/review/README.md; results/review/replay_validation.json; results/compute/pilot_summary.json. NVIDIA time is alignment only, excluding reference setup; no CPU speedup claim.

2:00–4:50
Here is the case that changed the next action. Psap–Lgals3 has six published read IDs and an RNA-model score of about 0.994. That score is not a biological probability. The pair is not listed as NanoString-supported, and per-probe QC is unknown.
The assistant compared the actual read endpoints with the sequence-mapped probe. The nearest second-parent endpoint differs by 924 nucleotides. We independently checked the source spreadsheets and reference transcript sequences using a separate coordinate implementation, and reproduced the discrepancy.
That does not prove an artifact or a bad probe. It tells us which uncertainty to resolve first: inspect the original alignment and coordinate convention before choosing a junction-specific assay. The real Parabricks subsample has no matching probe-junction reads; a bounded non-detection is not proof of absence.
[If browser available: show Psap case, choose Compare junctions, open recorded source, and show the review form without impersonating a scientist. Otherwise use the coordinate example on this slide.]
The two other cases show the same discipline: published RNA support can coexist with a low-confidence predicted structure, or with no structure at all.
We also tested Hi-C prioritization. Average precision moved from 0.296 to 0.300 on the matched cohort, with an interval spanning zero. We do not claim improved ranking or measured time savings. The contribution demonstrated is an inspectable evidence-review workflow with a concrete next decision. Independent biology review and prospective utility testing remain to be done.

Source: results/review/psap_source_audit.json and three frozen decisions; results/classifier/metrics.json. Three deliberately selected examples, not a blinded or random utility sample.
